mission: Cadenza Labs aims to reduce catastrophic risk from AI by publishing research and open tools for detecting AI dishonesty. It wants to help labs train more honest models and give regulators evidence about when safety interventions, or deeper (white-box) access, are needed.

key_work.title: Liars' Bench: Evaluating Lie Detectors for Language Models
key_work.plain_summary: A benchmark of many kinds of model lies for testing how well lie detectors work; Anthropic built on one of its settings.

key_work.title: Aletheia's Quest (with NDIF)
key_work.plain_summary: A lie-detection competition for language models run with NDIF and supported by Schmidt Sciences.

key_work.title: Cluster-Norm for Unsupervised Probing of Knowledge
key_work.plain_summary: Improves methods that try to read what a model 'knows' to be true without labelled data (EMNLP 2024).

key_work.title: Sleeper Agents replication
key_work.plain_summary: Open-source replication of Anthropic's sleeper-agent backdoor experiments.

warnings.text: Dishonest AI can hide what it is doing during training, evaluation and deployment.
Labs may claim black-box monitoring suffices when white-box access is actually needed.

recommendations.text: Build and benchmark dishonesty detectors for use in evaluations and monitoring.
Prefer training schemes that keep models amenable to monitoring, such as legible chain-of-thought.
Independently validate labs' claims about model honesty to prevent safety-washing.
